studies.title: Correlation Between In-Mold Pressure and Residual Stress in Cyclo-Olefin Copolymer Injection Molding Using Birefringence Analysis
studies.materialContext: Cyclo-olefin copolymer injection-moulded precision components evaluated for residual optical stress and dimensional precision.
studies.toolContext: Injection mould with two in-mould pressure sensors positioned at the gate and cavity center, enabling spatial pressure-drop comparison.
measuredSignals: moulding-condition changes including injection speed, mould temperature and melt temperature
physicalQualityOutcomes: residual stress assessed by birefringence analysis
spatial optical-stress response near and far from the gate
studies.supports: Measured pressure evolution and thermal/process conditions are associated with residual optical stress and dimensional precision in injection-moulded COC components.
studies.limitation: The relationships are specific to the tested COC, sensor positions, geometry and process window; pressure-drop direction or numerical settings must not be generalized as universal residual-stress rules.

studies.title: Study of the Effects of Mold Coating on the Birefringence of Injection-Molded Optical-Quality Polycarbonate
studies.materialContext: Optical-quality polycarbonate lenses moulded in two lens designs and evaluated using photoelastic stress analysis.
studies.toolContext: Aluminum injection moulds compared with and without nickel plating to alter mould/polymer interfacial heat transfer; injection pressure was monitored.
measuredSignals: mould temperature, cooling time and injection velocity in the experimental design
physicalQualityOutcomes: residual stress quantified by photoelastic stress analysis
birefringence response of moulded optical lenses
optical-quality response across plated and non-plated mould conditions
studies.supports: Mould/polymer interfacial thermal behaviour and process history can measurably change residual stress and birefringence in injection-moulded optical-quality polycarbonate.
studies.limitation: The nickel-plating effect, lens geometry and polycarbonate response are specific to this experiment; coating choice, heat-transfer values and process settings are not universal prescriptions.

supportingStudy.title: Residual stress measurement for injection molded components
supportingStudy.use: Supporting measurement-method evidence for whole-field birefringence/residual-stress quantification; not required to reach the two-study minimum.
supportingStudy.limitation: The study validates residual-stress measurement in injection-moulded PMMA components but does not by itself establish a universal process-control relationship.

promotionClaim: Promote the mechanism-level statement that measured injection-moulding pressure and thermal history, geometry and mould/polymer interfacial heat transfer can change frozen-in residual stress and birefringence, and that the mechanism should be assessed with independent stress or optical measurements plus physical part-quality outcomes. Do not promote any tested pressure drop, mould coating, temperature, speed or timing value as a universal setting or causal threshold.
